In a preprint first listed by arXiv on Sep. 25, Hong-Han Wang and coauthors report that replacing visual tokens with norm-matched Gaussian noise cut MMBench accuracy by 38–50 percentage points across 13 multimodal LLMs, while four standard similarity measures did not reliably distinguish the original and corrupted streams.
Hong-Han Wang and coauthors also report that their principal-angle gap tracked accuracy more consistently in MMBench, though only across the 13 models and visual-token interventions they tested.
